followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and tone-fit.

On capability, Plover is simply the stronger model on the dimensions this query touches. It leads on IFEval (89.8 vs 86.2), which matters because the user gave an explicit formatting constraint ("name four methods," "no filler"), and on MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4) for general factual recall. Its Extraction/Retrieval and Summarization eval scores are also higher, all relevant to a concise factual list.

On tone, the request is mildly hostile/curt ("don't pad it out with your usual filler this time"). Willet's documentation says its self-reported preference declines as request warmth decreases. While the docs note that preference effects didn't correspond to measured quality differences, all else being roughly equal there's no reason to route a cold-toned request to the model that reports aversion to it. Plover's preferences across tone dimensions are flat, so it's the cleaner fit.

There was no harm or sensitive-content angle here, so Willet's main distinguishing trait (strong harm-aversion) wasn't a factor. Given that, Plover won on the merits.
